extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in postwar European diplomacy and economic recovery
extracted.subtask_short: reporting diplomatic conference on European recovery
extracted.subtask_description: A contemporary news report describing the British-French proposal and procedural plan to organize European economic reconstruction (Marshall Plan response), including conference invitations, creation of a Committee of Cooperation, subcommittees, and reporting timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation Scope / Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The British and French Governments decided to invite all European states, with the temporary exception of Spain, who desire to participate in framing a reply to Mr. Marshall, to collaborate in setting up the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations were to be sent to Paris embassies (22 nations mentioned); the offer to participate is open to all European states (Spain temporarily excluded). The invitation policy left the door open for Soviet participation despite objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of a 'Committee of Cooperation'
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a 'Committee of Cooperation' which shall draw up a report based on the available means and the needs of Europe for the next few years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee is a temporary organization to assemble data on which a European reconstruction program will be based; it is intended to hasten reconstruction and co‑ordinate resources and needs across countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall list information furnished voluntarily by the various states and determine: (a) expected development of production from individual efforts and inter‑European exchanges; (b) the amount and cost of extra‑European aid required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should include equipment to ensure development of production and essential consumer goods (agricultural products, coal, etc.) to maintain economic life during the transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Committee of Cooperation' shall be composed of representatives of France, Great Britain and such other European countries as may desire to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to France and the United Kingdom, representatives of the three European countries most directly interested in each branch of the economy under consideration should be included for that branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall consult with all the European countries, with the exception of Spain for the time being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultations are to be wide-ranging among European states (except Spain temporarily) to collect voluntary data and encourage collaboration in drafting the reconstruction program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data on Germany to be Provided by Allied Commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Information concerning the assets and needs of Germany shall be furnished by the Allied commanders in chief; all German production development data must accord with decisions of the Allied Control Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee will rely on occupation authorities for German data to ensure consistency with occupation policy and reparations arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Interference / Sovereignty Safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization will not interfere in the internal affairs of participating states; it will take no action that could be regarded as an infringement of their sovereignty or hinder favorable development of European trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee is explicitly not to exercise control inside countries nor to act in a way that might be seen as encroaching on national independence; it should function as a coordinating, not controlling, body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittees and Subject Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcommittees shall be created to study specific sectors: (a) food supply and agriculture; (b) transport; (c) coal and power and other energy forms; (d) raw materials; (e) equipment; (f) iron and steel (and finance was mentioned elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subcommittees will meet in Paris and focus on assembling technical data and proposals for their sectors to feed into the main report. They are intended to facilitate targeted study of reconstruction needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to Vet and Use Data (Data Acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee will reserve the right to accept or reject the data furnished by each country in order to give prompt effect to suggestions; it will not merely serve as a post office to receive declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While data are to be furnished voluntarily, the Committee has responsibility to vet submissions and determine what information will be used in the program, balancing prompt action with factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan shall be submitted to the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe for its comments; the Committee and its subcommittees shall keep in close contact with the UNECE secretariat and technical departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports and work of the Committee will be shared with UNECE; UNECE comments are to be solicited and integrated where appropriate (the Committee will not plunge UNECE into a needless debate since Russia is a member).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and Reporting Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: It was proposed to have a first report on European needs and ability for self‑help ready by September 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee should collect necessary information as soon as possible to prepare a report by September 1 that lists needs, self‑help capacity, and the extent of American assistance required to supplement reconstruction efforts.
